blocks.en: After studying this unit you will be able to craft a clear, biblical invitation and appeal that calls listeners to immediate decision for Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Después de estudiar esta unidad podrá elaborar una invitación y un llamado claros y bíblicos que llamen a los oyentes a una decisión inmediata por Cristo.

blocks.en: The Importance of the Invitation and Appeal
blocks.es_reference: La Importancia de la Invitación y el Llamado

blocks.en: Every evangelistic sermon must end with a clear invitation and appeal. The invitation is the moment the preacher asks the listener to respond to the gospel. The appeal is the urgent call that presses the heart to decide today. WiseSpeak teaches that without a strong invitation the sermon remains incomplete. The listener may understand the truth but never take the step of faith. A well-crafted invitation turns knowledge into action.
blocks.es_reference: Cada sermón evangelístico debe terminar con una invitación y un llamado claros. La invitación es el momento en que el predicador pide al oyente que responda al evangelio. El llamado es el urgente ruego que presiona el corazón a decidir hoy. WiseSpeak enseña que sin una fuerte invitación el sermón queda incompleto. El oyente puede entender la verdad pero nunca dar el paso de fe. Una invitación bien elaborada convierte el conocimiento en acción.

blocks.en: The Keyword Method Carries Through
blocks.es_reference: El Método de la Palabra Clave Continúa

blocks.en: The invitation and appeal must be biblical, personal, and urgent. They flow naturally from the keyword approach used in the first seven units of WiseSpeak: the invitation uses the sermon's own keyword to call for a definite response. The invitation and appeal keep the same keyword so the entire sermon feels unified from beginning to end.
blocks.es_reference: La invitación y el llamado deben ser bíblicos, personales y urgentes. Fluyen naturalmente del enfoque de la palabra clave usado en las primeras siete unidades de WiseSpeak: la invitación usa la propia palabra clave del sermón para llamar a una respuesta definida. La invitación y el llamado mantienen la misma palabra clave para que todo el sermón se sienta unificado del principio al fin.

blocks.en: How to Craft the Invitation and Appeal
blocks.es_reference: Cómo Elaborar la Invitación y el Llamado

blocks.en: Finish the main points of the sermon.
blocks.es_reference: Terminar los puntos principales del sermón.

blocks.en: Restate the probing question the text answers.
blocks.es_reference: Repetir la pregunta de sondeo que el texto responde.

blocks.en: Review the plural noun keyword that holds the sermon together.
blocks.es_reference: Revisar la palabra clave (sustantivo plural) que mantiene unido el sermón.

blocks.en: Form the subject around the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Formar el tema alrededor de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: Write three short parallel points (each five words or less) that are singulars of the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: Escribir tres puntos cortos y paralelos (cada uno de cinco palabras o menos) que sean singulares de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: Craft a one-sentence evangelistic objective that calls for immediate decision.
blocks.es_reference: Elaborar un objetivo evangelístico de una sola oración que llame a una decisión inmediata.

blocks.en: Prepare the actual invitation words and the appeal that follows.
blocks.es_reference: Preparar las palabras reales de la invitación y el llamado que sigue.

blocks.en: Worked Example — John 3:16
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo Trabajado — Juan 3:16

blocks.en: The subject is "Three Reasons God Sent His Son."
blocks.es_reference: El tema es "Tres Razones por las que Dios Envió a Su Hijo".

blocks.en: Question: Why did God send His Son? · Keyword: reasons
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Por qué envió Dios a Su Hijo? · Palabra clave: razones

blocks.en: Show His love.
blocks.es_reference: Mostrar Su amor.

blocks.en: Offer eternal life.
blocks.es_reference: Ofrecer vida eterna.

blocks.en: Save the world.
blocks.es_reference: Salvar al mundo.

blocks.en: Objective: "To lead every listener to accept God's reasons by believing in Jesus Christ today."
blocks.es_reference: Objetivo: "Llevar a cada oyente a aceptar las razones de Dios creyendo en Jesucristo hoy".

blocks.en: "Today you have heard three reasons God sent His Son. He sent His Son to show His love. He sent His Son to offer eternal life. He sent His Son to save the world. Right now, in this moment, will you believe in Jesus Christ and receive the eternal life He offers? If you will, simply stand where you are or come forward as we sing. The decision is yours. The time is now."
blocks.es_reference: "Hoy has escuchado tres razones por las que Dios envió a Su Hijo. Él envió a Su Hijo para mostrar Su amor. Él envió a Su Hijo para ofrecer vida eterna. Él envió a Su Hijo para salvar al mundo. En este mismo momento, ¿creerás en Jesucristo y recibirás la vida eterna que Él ofrece? Si lo harás, simplemente ponte de pie donde estás o ven al frente mientras cantamos. La decisión es tuya. El tiempo es ahora".

blocks.en: The invitation is short, direct, and calls for immediate response.
blocks.es_reference: La invitación es corta, directa y llama a una respuesta inmediata.

blocks.en: Worked Example — Acts 16:30–31
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo Trabajado — Hechos 16:30–31

blocks.en: The subject is "Three Steps to Salvation."
blocks.es_reference: El tema es "Tres Pasos para la Salvación".

blocks.en: Question: What must I do to be saved? · Keyword: steps
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Qué debo hacer para ser salvo? · Palabra clave: pasos

blocks.en: Hear the gospel.
blocks.es_reference: Escuchar el evangelio.

blocks.en: Believe in Jesus.
blocks.es_reference: Creer en Jesús.

blocks.en: Be baptized.
blocks.es_reference: Ser bautizado.

blocks.en: Objective: "To lead every listener to take God's steps by believing in Jesus Christ today."
blocks.es_reference: Objetivo: "Llevar a cada oyente a dar los pasos de Dios creyendo en Jesucristo hoy".

blocks.en: "You have heard three steps to salvation. The first step is to hear the gospel. The second step is to believe in Jesus. The third step is to be baptized. Which step will you take right now? If you are ready to believe in Jesus, stand with me as we pray together. The decision is yours. The time is now."
blocks.es_reference: "Has escuchado tres pasos para la salvación. El primer paso es escuchar el evangelio. El segundo paso es creer en Jesús. El tercer paso es ser bautizado. ¿Cuál paso darás ahora mismo? Si estás listo para creer en Jesús, ponte de pie conmigo mientras oramos juntos. La decisión es tuya. El tiempo es ahora".

blocks.en: Worked Example — Romans 10:9
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplo Trabajado — Romanos 10:9

blocks.en: The subject is "God's Conditions for Salvation."
blocks.es_reference: El tema es "Las Condiciones de Dios para la Salvación".

blocks.en: Question: How can I be saved? · Keyword: conditions
blocks.es_reference: Pregunta: ¿Cómo puedo ser salvo? · Palabra clave: condiciones

blocks.en: Confess with your mouth.
blocks.es_reference: Confesar con la boca.

blocks.en: Believe in your heart.
blocks.es_reference: Creer en el corazón.

blocks.en: Receive God's salvation.
blocks.es_reference: Recibir la salvación de Dios.

blocks.en: Objective: "To lead every listener to meet God's conditions by believing in Jesus Christ today."
blocks.es_reference: Objetivo: "Llevar a cada oyente a cumplir las condiciones de Dios creyendo en Jesucristo hoy".

blocks.en: "God has given three conditions for salvation. You must confess with your mouth. You must believe in your heart. You must receive God's salvation. Will you meet these conditions right now? If your answer is yes, come forward as we sing. The decision is yours. The time is now."
blocks.es_reference: "Dios ha dado tres condiciones para la salvación. Debes confesar con la boca. Debes creer en el corazón. Debes recibir la salvación de Dios. ¿Cumplirás estas condiciones ahora mismo? Si tu respuesta es sí, ven al frente mientras cantamos. La decisión es tuya. El tiempo es ahora".

blocks.en: Why a Strong Invitation and Appeal Matter
blocks.es_reference: Por Qué Importa una Fuerte Invitación y Llamado

blocks.en: A strong invitation and appeal turn the sermon into a personal conversation with the listener. They move the message from the head to the heart. They give the Holy Spirit a clear moment to work. The plural noun keyword keeps the invitation connected to the entire sermon. Together they create urgency without pressure and clarity without confusion.
blocks.es_reference: Una fuerte invitación y llamado convierten el sermón en una conversación personal con el oyente. Mueven el mensaje de la cabeza al corazón. Dan al Espíritu Santo un momento claro para obrar. La palabra clave (sustantivo plural) mantiene la invitación conectada a todo el sermón. Juntos crean urgencia sin presión y claridad sin confusión.

blocks.en: Practical Steps to Craft Your Own Invitation and Appeal
blocks.es_reference: Pasos Prácticos para Elaborar tu Propia Invitación y Llamado

blocks.en: Work through the seven steps above for your own sermon. Then practice the invitation and appeal out loud until they feel natural. These steps, taken from the planning methods taught in WiseSpeak, give every evangelistic sermon a powerful conclusion.
blocks.es_reference: Seguir los siete pasos de arriba para el propio sermón. Luego practicar la invitación y el llamado en voz alta hasta que se sientan naturales. Estos pasos, tomados de los métodos de planificación enseñados en WiseSpeak, dan a cada sermón evangelístico una conclusión poderosa.

mc.stem: What does the invitation do in an evangelistic sermon?
options: Provides the offering appeal for the closing minutes
Summarizes the historical setting of the passage
Lists the church's denominational distinctives
Asks the listener to respond to the gospel

mc.stem: The appeal is best described as:
options: A polite suggestion the listener may consider later
The urgent call that presses the heart to decide today
A summary of doctrines for theological discussion
A philosophical reflection on the gospel

mc.stem: Without a strong invitation, WiseSpeak teaches that the sermon:
options: Becomes purely doctrinal in nature
Is fully complete in itself
Remains incomplete
Cannot be preached again

mc.stem: The invitation and appeal must be:
options: Biblical, personal, and urgent
Vague, optional, and casual
Long, scholarly, and footnoted
Anonymous, indirect, and quiet

mc.stem: The keyword used through the invitation method must always be:
options: A verb in the imperative
A plural noun
A proper name from the passage
An adjective describing the listener

mc.stem: In the John 3:16 example, the keyword chosen is:
options: reasons
conditions
proofs
steps

mc.stem: In the John 3:16 example, the three points are:
options: Living water; True worship; Personal testimony
Hear the gospel; Believe in Jesus; Be baptized
Confess with mouth; Believe in heart; Receive salvation
Show His love; Offer eternal life; Save the world

mc.stem: In the Acts 16:30–31 example, the keyword chosen is:
options: reasons
conditions
steps
proofs

mc.stem: In the Acts 16:30–31 example, the three points are:
options: Hear the gospel; Believe in Jesus; Be baptized
Show His love; Offer eternal life; Save the world
Confess with mouth; Believe in heart; Receive salvation
Father's love; Open arms; Full restoration

mc.stem: In the Romans 10:9 example, the keyword chosen is:
options: reasons
steps
proofs
conditions

mc.stem: The Romans 10:9 sample invitation calls for the listener to:
options: Hear, believe, and be baptized
Confess with the mouth, believe in the heart, and receive God's salvation
Reflect privately and discuss it next week
Wait until the next service for a response

mc.stem: The phrase repeated at the end of all three sample invitations is:
options: "Lord, have mercy on us all"
"Glory to God forever"
"The decision is yours. The time is now."
"We will meet again next Sunday"

mc.stem: What is the FIRST of the seven steps for crafting the invitation and appeal?
options: Prepare the actual invitation words
Finish the main points of the sermon
Write the one-sentence evangelistic objective
Restate the probing question the text answers

mc.stem: The one-sentence evangelistic objective in the invitation method aims at:
options: Filling the offering plate
Comforting the saints with assurance
Defending doctrine against critics
A definite, immediate decision

mc.stem: A strong invitation and appeal turn the sermon into:
options: A personal conversation with the listener
A theological lecture for trained scholars
A musical performance for emotional effect
A historical reenactment of the early church

mc.stem: Together the invitation and appeal create:
options: Pressure without urgency and confusion without clarity
Entertainment without depth and noise without unity
Urgency without pressure and clarity without confusion
Memorization without understanding and unity without urgency

mc.stem: What length should each outline point be in the invitation method?
options: A full sentence of any length
Five words or less
Ten words or less
As long as needed for theological accuracy

mc.stem: Why does the invitation keep the same keyword used through the sermon?
options: So the entire sermon feels unified from beginning to end
To allow the preacher to switch keywords mid-sermon
To match the church's denominational creed
To shorten the time required for preparation

mc.stem: What does this unit say a well-crafted invitation does for the listener?
options: Eliminates the need for follow-up discipleship
Replaces the need for the Holy Spirit's work
Substitutes for personal prayer at home
Turns knowledge into action

mc.stem: In the worked examples, the sample invitations include practical instructions such as:
options: Memorizing the entire sermon outline before responding
Reading the original Greek alongside the English text
Standing where they are, coming forward, or standing with the preacher to pray
Donating sacrificially to the church building fund first

sa.prompt: Define both the invitation and the appeal in your own words.
sa.model: The invitation is the moment the preacher asks the listener to respond to the gospel; the appeal is the urgent call that presses the heart to decide today. Together they turn knowledge into action and complete the evangelistic sermon.

sa.prompt: List the seven steps for crafting the invitation and appeal.
sa.model: The seven steps are: finish the sermon body, recall the probing question and keyword, restate the subject and points, state the objective, give the invitation, press the appeal, and call for an immediate response.

sa.prompt: In the John 3:16 example, what is the question, what is the keyword, what are the three points, and what does the sample invitation call the listener to do?
sa.model: In the John 3:16 example the question is 'Why did God send His Son?', the keyword is 'reasons,' and the points are show His love, offer eternal life, save the world; the invitation asks the listener to believe and come forward today.

sa.prompt: In the Acts 16:30–31 example, what is the question, what is the keyword, what are the three points, and what does the sample invitation call the listener to do?
sa.model: In the Acts 16:30-31 example the question is 'What must I do to be saved?', the keyword is 'steps,' and the points are hear the gospel, believe in Jesus, be baptized; the invitation asks the listener to stand and pray to receive Christ.

sa.prompt: In the Romans 10:9 example, what is the question, what is the keyword, what are the three points, and what does the sample invitation call the listener to do?
sa.model: In the Romans 10:9 example the question is 'How can I be saved?', the keyword is 'conditions,' and the points are confess with your mouth, believe in your heart, receive God's salvation; the invitation calls the listener to come forward and confess Christ.

sa.prompt: Why does this unit say a strong invitation and appeal matter? Give at least two reasons.
sa.model: A strong invitation and appeal matter for at least two reasons: they move the truth from the head to the heart and call for action, and they give the Holy Spirit a clear, unified moment to press for a decision so the listener actually responds rather than just understanding.

sa.prompt: Explain the kind of closing the sample invitations share and why pressing the listener that the decision is his and the time is now is important.
sa.model: The sample invitations all close by pressing that the decision is the listener's own and the time is now. This urgency matters because it refuses to let the listener delay; it calls for an immediate, personal response to Christ today rather than someday.

sa.prompt: State the keyword rule and the points rule that govern the invitation method.
sa.model: The invitation method is governed by the same rules: the keyword is a plural noun, and every point is a short, parallel singular of that keyword, five words or less, so the closing stays unified with the sermon.

sa.prompt: According to this unit, what does a well-crafted invitation do for the listener?
sa.model: A well-crafted invitation turns knowledge into action: it moves the listener from merely understanding the truth to taking the step of faith and making a decision to respond to Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain the twin qualities the invitation and appeal create together, and why both are needed without tipping into manipulation.
sa.model: Together the invitation and appeal create urgency and clarity: clarity so the listener knows exactly how to respond, and urgency so he feels the call to respond now. Both are needed, but they must stay biblical and honest, pressing for decision without manipulation.
